Neem.name: Neem
side_effects: May cause mild dryness or irritation on extremely sensitive skin if used undiluted
contraindications: Extremely dry skin conditions (use with a hydrating carrier)
research_papers: Alzohairy MA. Therapeutics Role of Azadirachta indica (Neem) and Their Active Constituents in Diseases Prevention and Treatment. Evid Based Complement Alternat Med. 2016.
Kumar VS, Navaratnam V. Neem (Azadirachta indica): Prehistory to contemporary medicinal uses to humankind. Asian Pac J Trop Biomed. 2013.
Neem.preparation_method: Grind fresh neem leaves with water to form a paste and apply to affected areas, or dilute neem oil (2-3 drops) in coconut oil.

Aloe Vera.name: Aloe Vera
side_effects: Rare allergic contact dermatitis in sensitive individuals
research_papers: Surjushe A, Vasani R, Saple DG. Aloe vera: a short review. Indian J Dermatol. 2008.
Hekmatpou D, et al. Effect of Aloe Vera Clinical Trials on Skin Prevention and Healing: A Systematic Review. Iran J Med Sci. 2019.
Aloe Vera.preparation_method: Extract fresh gel from an Aloe leaf and apply directly to the skin. No dilution required.

Turmeric.name: Turmeric
side_effects: Temporary yellow skin staining
Mild contact dermatitis in rare cases
contraindications: None major, but avoid applying to fresh open bleeding wounds
research_papers: Vaughn AR, Branum A, Sivamani RK. Effects of Turmeric (Curcuma longa) on Skin Health: A Systematic Review of the Clinical Evidence. Phytother Res. 2016.
Turmeric.preparation_method: Mix 1/2 teaspoon of turmeric powder with yogurt or honey to form a paste. Apply for 10-15 minutes and rinse.

Tulsi.name: Tulsi
side_effects: Generally very safe; mild warming sensation on application
research_papers: Cohen MM. Tulsi - Ocimum sanctum: A herb for all reasons. J Ayurveda Integr Med. 2014.
Tulsi.preparation_method: Crush tulsi leaves and extract the juice. Apply this juice directly using a cotton ball to acne lesions.

Amla.name: Amla
side_effects: Highly acidic; might cause mild tingling on sensitive skin
research_papers: Fujii T, et al. Amla (Emblica officinalis Gaertn.) extract promotes procollagen production and inhibits matrix metalloproteinase-1 in human skin fibroblasts. J Ethnopharmacol. 2008.
Amla.preparation_method: Mix amla powder with raw honey or rose water, apply as a mask for 10 minutes, then wash off.

Harra.name: Harra
side_effects: Can cause dryness due to high tannin content
contraindications: Extremely dry skin (always combine with a lipid carrier)
research_papers: Bag A, et al. The development of Terminalia chebula Retz. (Combretaceae) in clinical research. Asian Pac J Trop Biomed. 2013.
Harra.preparation_method: Make a fine paste of Harra powder with water and apply as a spot treatment on minor wounds or rashes.

Bahera.name: Bahera
side_effects: Mild drying effect
research_papers: Saraswathi V, et al. Antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity of Terminalia bellirica. Journal of Pharmacy Research. 2012.
Bahera.preparation_method: Mix Bahera powder with warm water, apply as a paste on inflamed or swollen skin patches.

Giloy.name: Giloy
side_effects: Generally extremely safe; no significant topical side effects
research_papers: Saha S, Ghosh S. Tinospora cordifolia: One plant, many roles. Anc Sci Life. 2012.
Giloy.preparation_method: Boil Giloy stems in water to prepare a decoction, let it cool, and wash the affected skin areas.

Mahua.name: Mahua
side_effects: Can feel heavy or greasy; may clog pores on oily skin
contraindications: Active acne-prone skin (due to high lipid content)
research_papers: Ramadan MF, et al. Bioactive lipids and phytochemicals of Madhuca longifolia seed oil. Food Chemistry. 2006.
Mahua.preparation_method: Apply cold-pressed Mahua seed oil directly onto patches of dry skin, or mix with beeswax to form a salve.

Karanj.name: Karanj
side_effects: Strong smell; may cause warmth or mild burning sensation initially
contraindications: Do not apply to open bleeding lesions
research_papers: Ramesh M, et al. Antifungal and antibacterial activity of Pongamia pinnata (Karanj) seed oil. Fitoterapia. 2002.
Karanj.preparation_method: Dilute Karanj oil with neem oil or coconut oil in a 1:5 ratio and apply to affected patches.

Palash.name: Palash
side_effects: Palash flower extract may dye the skin temporarily orange
research_papers: Mishra M, et al. Butea monosperma (Palash): A review on its phytochemical and pharmacological profile. Int J Phytomed. 2011.
Palash.preparation_method: Infuse Palash flowers in hot water to create a soothing rinse, or crush flowers into a paste.

Moringa.name: Moringa
side_effects: Very well tolerated; extremely low incidence of reactions
research_papers: Ali A, et al. Enhancement of human skin facial revitalization by moringa leaf extract cream. Postepy Dermatol Alergol. 2014.
Moringa.preparation_method: Apply cold-pressed Moringa seed oil as a moisturizer or face oil, or make a leaf powder paste.

Hibiscus.name: Hibiscus
side_effects: Mild tingling due to natural fruit acids
contraindications: Raw applying on sunburns or fresh peeling skin
research_papers: Nanda A, et al. Evaluation of cosmetic potential of Hibiscus rosa-sinensis petals. Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology. 2019.
Hibiscus.preparation_method: Crush fresh hibiscus petals with a little yogurt, apply to face for 15 minutes, then rinse with warm water.

Ashwagandha.name: Ashwagandha
side_effects: Very rare contact allergy
research_papers: Sikandar M, et al. Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) in skincare: Clinical studies and phytochemical insights. Phytotherapy Letters. 2021.
Ashwagandha.preparation_method: Mix Ashwagandha root powder with ghee or honey and apply to areas showing fine lines or fatigue.

Bael.name: Bael
side_effects: May cause slight dryness if used excessively
contraindications: Very dry skin without mixing with oils
research_papers: Bhalodia NR, Shukla VJ. Antibacterial and wound healing properties of Aegle marmelos fruit extracts. J Adv Pharm Technol Res. 2011.
Bael.preparation_method: Mash the pulp of ripe Bael fruit, apply to irritated skin patch, let sit for 15 minutes, wash off.

Arjun.name: Arjun
side_effects: Mild astringent drying effect
research_papers: Chaudhari M, et al. Terminalia arjuna bark extract: barrier repair and microcirculation benefits in skin care. Journal of Ethnopharmacology. 2014.
Arjun.preparation_method: Mix Arjun bark powder with honey and milk to make a skin paste. Apply twice a week.

Chironji.name: Chironji
side_effects: Comedogenic risk for highly oily acne-prone skin
research_papers: Siddiqui AA, et al. Phytochemical and therapeutic potential of Buchanania lanzan (Chironji) seeds. Journal of Natural Remedies. 2015.
Chironji.preparation_method: Grind Chironji seeds with milk to make a paste, apply on skin for soft texture and fading of dry patches.

Bhringraj.name: Bhringraj
side_effects: Very high tolerance rate; no common side effects reported
research_papers: Tewtrakul S, et al. Anti-inflammatory and wound healing activities of Eclipta prostrata. Journal of Ethnopharmacology. 2011.
Bhringraj.preparation_method: Extract juice from crushed fresh Bhringraj leaves and apply to wounds, or apply Bhringraj leaf powder paste.

Brahmi.name: Brahmi
Brahmi.preparation_method: Apply Brahmi paste made from fresh leaves or use Brahmi oil for topical massage.
side_effects: Mild stomach upset if ingested in large quantities
research_papers: Stough C, et al. Bacopa monnieri improves human memory. J Altern Complement Med. 2001.

Castor.name: Castor
Castor.preparation_method: Apply cold-pressed castor oil directly to skin or mix with carrier oil.
side_effects: May clog pores for oily skin types
research_papers: Oh JW, et al. Castor oil: a review of pharmacology and toxicology. J Toxicol. 2014.

Curry_Leaf.name: Curry Leaf
Curry_Leaf.preparation_method: Crush fresh curry leaves into a paste and apply to skin, or use curry leaf infused oil.
side_effects: Generally very safe for topical use
research_papers: Nadkarni KM, et al. Indian Materia Medica. 1976.

Doddapatre.name: Doddapatre
Doddapatre.preparation_method: Use fresh Doddapatre leaves as a paste or infuse in water for a skin rinse.
side_effects: Mild tingling sensation on sensitive skin
research_papers: Indian Ayurvedic texts on Coleus aromaticus

Ekka.name: Ekka
Ekka.preparation_method: Apply Ekka leaf paste to affected areas. Use with caution and under guidance.
side_effects: Can cause skin irritation in sensitive individuals
contraindications: Do not use on open wounds without medical supervision
research_papers: Khare CP, et al. Indian Medicinal Plants. 2007.

Ganike.name: Ganike
Ganike.preparation_method: Apply Ganike fruit paste or use Ganike leaf decoction for skin application.
side_effects: Mild skin irritation possible
research_papers: Indian Ayurvedic texts on Solanum xanthocarpum

Gauva.name: Gauva
Gauva.preparation_method: Apply Guava leaf paste or use Guava leaf decoction as a skin toner.
side_effects: Generally very safe for topical use
research_papers: Dua P, et al. Psidium guajava: A review. Pharmacogn Rev. 2011.

Geranium.name: Geranium
Geranium.preparation_method: Use geranium essential oil diluted in a carrier oil for massage, or apply geranium-infused water as a toner.
side_effects: Mild skin irritation possible with undiluted oil
research_papers: Diniz SO, et al. Phytochemical and pharmacological profile of Pelargonium. 2019.

Henna.name: Henna
Henna.preparation_method: Apply henna paste made from dried henna leaves mixed with water or lemon juice.
side_effects: Skin staining that lasts 1-2 weeks
Mild allergic reactions possible
contraindications: Do a patch test before use
research_papers: Inamdar AA, et al. Lawsonia inermis: an ethnopharmacological review. Pharmacogn Rev. 2011.

Honge.name: Honge
Honge.preparation_method: Apply Honge oil (diluted) to affected skin areas. Mix with coconut oil before use.
side_effects: Strong smell; may cause mild burning sensation
contraindications: Do not apply to open bleeding lesions
research_papers: Ramesh M, et al. Antifungal activity of Pongamia pinnata seed oil. Fitoterapia. 2002.

Insulin.name: Insulin Plant
Insulin.preparation_method: Chew fresh Insulin plant leaves or apply leaf paste to skin for wound healing.
side_effects: Mild gastrointestinal discomfort if consumed in excess
contraindications: Diabetic patients should monitor blood sugar when using
research_papers: Indian traditional medicine texts on Costus igneus

Jasmine.name: Jasmine
Jasmine.preparation_method: Use jasmine essential oil diluted in a carrier oil, or apply jasmine-infused water as a toner.
side_effects: Mild skin irritation possible with undiluted oil
research_papers: Trotin F, et al. Antioxidant properties of Jasminum officinale. 2003.

Lemon.name: Lemon
Lemon.preparation_method: Apply fresh lemon juice diluted with water to skin, or use lemon-infused honey mask.
side_effects: Photosensitivity - avoid sun exposure after application
Mild stinging on sensitive skin
contraindications: Do not apply before sun exposure
Avoid on broken or irritated skin
research_papers: Kumar S, et al. Citrus limon: A review. Pharmacogn Rev. 2008.

Lemon_grass.name: Lemon Grass
Lemon_grass.preparation_method: Use lemon grass essential oil diluted in a carrier oil, or apply lemon grass infusion as a skin toner.
side_effects: Mild skin irritation possible with undiluted oil
research_papers: Santos-Buelga C, et al. Phytochemical analysis of Cymbopogon citratus. 2014.

Mango.name: Mango
Mango.preparation_method: Apply mango pulp directly to skin as a mask, or use mango butter for moisturizing.
side_effects: Mild allergic reaction possible in sensitive individuals
research_papers: Siddiqui IA, et al. Mangifera indica: A review. Pharmacogn Rev. 2012.

Mint.name: Mint
Mint.preparation_method: Apply fresh mint leaf paste to skin, or use mint-infused water as a toner.
side_effects: Mild cooling sensation may be intense on sensitive skin
contraindications: Avoid on broken or irritated skin
research_papers: McKay DL, et al. Mentha spicata: A review. J Tradit Complement Med. 2014.

Nagadali.name: Nagadali
Nagadali.preparation_method: Apply Manjistha root powder paste to skin, or use Manjistha-infused water as a skin tonic.
side_effects: Mild skin irritation possible
contraindications: Pregnancy should consult doctor before use
research_papers: Aggarwal BB, et al. Curcuma longa: A review. 2007.

Nithyapushpa.name: Nithyapushpa
Nithyapushpa.preparation_method: Apply fresh Nithyapushpa leaf paste to skin, or use leaf-infused water as a toner.
side_effects: Mild skin irritation possible
research_papers: Traditional Ayurvedic texts on Tradescantia

Nooni.name: Nooni
Nooni.preparation_method: Apply Nooni fruit paste or use Nooni bark decoction as a skin wash.
side_effects: Mild drying effect
research_papers: Indian Ayurvedic texts on Ziziphus mauritiana

Pappaya.name: Pappaya
Pappaya.preparation_method: Apply fresh papaya pulp as a face mask, or use papaya enzyme powder mixed with honey.
side_effects: Mild tingling or irritation possible on sensitive skin
contraindications: Avoid on broken or irritated skin
research_papers: Purnima S, et al. Carica papaya: A review. Pharmacogn Rev. 2010.

Pepper.name: Pepper
Pepper.preparation_method: Use diluted black pepper essential oil in a carrier oil for massage, or apply pepper-infused water.
side_effects: Burning sensation on sensitive skin
Photosensitivity
contraindications: Do not use undiluted essential oil
research_papers: Srinivasan K. Piper nigrum (black pepper): A review. Crit Rev Food Sci Nutr. 2007.

Pomegranate.name: Pomegranate
Pomegranate.preparation_method: Apply pomegranate seed oil or fresh pomegranate juice to skin, or use pomegranate extract serum.
side_effects: Mild stomach upset if consumed in excess
research_papers: Seeram NP, et al. Pomegranate: A review of its anti-inflammatory and skin benefits. 2010.

Raktachandini.name: Raktachandini
Raktachandini.preparation_method: Apply Raktachandini powder paste to skin, or use decoction as a skin wash.
side_effects: Mild skin irritation possible
contraindications: Pregnancy should consult doctor before use
research_papers: Indian Ayurvedic texts on Pterocarpus santalinus

Rose.name: Rose
Rose.preparation_method: Use rose water as a skin toner, or apply rose essential oil diluted in a carrier oil.
side_effects: Mild skin irritation possible with undiluted oil
research_papers: Koulivand PH, et al. Rosa damascena: A review. Complement Ther Med. 2013.

Sapota.name: Sapota
Sapota.preparation_method: Apply fresh Sapota fruit pulp as a face mask, or use Sapota seed oil for moisturizing.

Wood_sorel.preparation_method: Apply fresh Wood Sorel leaf paste to skin, or use leaf infusion as a skin wash.

Arali.preparation_method: Apply Arali root powder paste to skin, or use root decoction as a skin wash.

Ashoka.preparation_method: Apply Ashoka bark decoction to skin, or use Ashoka flower paste for skin care.

Avocado.name: Avocado
Avocado.preparation_method: Apply mashed avocado pulp directly to skin as a mask, or use avocado oil for moisturizing.

Bamboo.preparation_method: Apply bamboo leaf decoction to skin, or use bamboo silica extract as a skin treatment.

Basale.name: Basale
Basale.preparation_method: Apply fresh Basale leaf paste to skin, or use leaf infusion as a skin wash.

Betel.name: Betel
Betel.preparation_method: Apply fresh Betel leaf paste to skin, or use Betel leaf decoction as a skin wash.

research_papers: Indian Ayurvedic texts on Piper betle

Bakuchi.name: Bakuchi
benefits: Traditionally used in preparations for vitiligo and other depigmentation-related skin conditions
Contains photosensitizing compounds that have been studied in relation to repigmentation approaches
Has demonstrated anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities in experimental studies
Bakuchi.preparation_method: Use only under the guidance of a qualified healthcare professional. Bakuchi preparations, particularly seed or seed-oil preparations, should not be self-applied because photosensitivity and other adverse effects have been reported.
side_effects: Photosensitivity
Erythema
Skin irritation
Blistering
Itching
Potential liver injury with systemic or prolonged use
contraindications: Avoid unsupervised use in people with liver disease
Avoid unsupervised use in people with known photosensitivity or conditions associated with light sensitivity
Avoid direct exposure to sunlight or ultraviolet radiation after topical use unless specifically directed by a qualified healthcare professional
Pregnancy and breastfeeding require professional medical advice before use
research_papers: Psoralea corylifolia L.: a comprehensive review of its botany, traditional uses, phytochemistry, pharmacology, toxicology, quality control and pharmacokinetics (PMID: 36627680)
Psoralea corylifolia L: Ethnobotanical, biological, and chemical aspects: A review (PMID: 29243333)
The Safety of Medicinal Plants Used in the Treatment of Vitiligo and Hypermelanosis: A Systematic Review of Use and Reports of Harm (PMID: 33790609)
Bakuchi.evidence_level: Traditional use with limited clinical evidence; safety concerns require professional supervision

Betel Nut.preparation_method: Apply Betel nut powder paste to skin, or use Betel nut decoction as a skin wash.
side_effects: Mild skin irritation possible
Can be drying
